title: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti
hook: Duryodhana and Arjuna arrive at Krishna's bedside on the same errand, and where each one sits decides who is seen first
carry: whose face Krishna saw when he opened his eyes
tomorrow: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti

segments.voice: Yesterday the masks came off in King Virata's court, and Arjuna gave the princess he taught to his son. Your line was the teacher stays a teacher. Who did you give credit to? Day eight hundred thirteen.
screen: `VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.` · `THE MASKS COME OFF.`

segments.voice: Two cousins walk into the same bedroom, a few moments apart. Krishna is asleep in his palace at Dwaraka. Duryodhana arrives first. He takes a fine seat at the head of the bed. Arjuna comes in after him, and stands at the foot of the bed, hands folded. Both have come for the same thing: Krishna's help in the war that now looks likely. Both wait. Krishna wakes, and the first person his eyes fall on is Arjuna. Today a new book of the epic begins, the Udyoga, and it opens with a choice.
screen: `TWO COUSINS, ONE ERRAND.` → `THE HEAD OF THE BED, THE FOOT.` → `WHO IS SEEN FIRST?`

segments.voice: Udyoga is a Sanskrit word for effort, for getting ready. The name fits. This book is all preparation: for peace, if it can be found, and for war, if it can't. It started in Virata's hall, where the families talked it through. Balarama, Krishna's brother, said the Pandavas should ask gently, since Yudhishthira had chosen to play that game. Satyaki answered him hotly. King Drupada said: send an envoy, and gather allies too. So both sides go looking for friends, and both end up at Krishna's bed. Krishna makes them an offer. On one side, a huge army of his own fighting men. On the other, Krishna himself, alone, and he will not take up a weapon in the fight. Arjuna, he says, may choose first. He saw him first, and he's the younger. Arjuna doesn't hesitate. He chooses Krishna, unarmed. Duryodhana is delighted. He gets the army, and he leaves thinking he's won the better half of the bargain. Now think about what each cousin was really asking for. Duryodhana wanted strength he could count. Arjuna wanted the person. And look back at the bedroom. Duryodhana sat at the head, where a guest of rank sits. Arjuna stood at the feet, the way you stand before someone you honor. Nobody in the story says the seat decided it. The story just shows us where each man chose to be, and whose face Krishna saw when he opened his eyes.
screen: `UDYOGA: EFFORT, GETTING READY` · `THE COUNCIL IN VIRATA'S HALL` · `AN ARMY, OR KRISHNA UNARMED` · then, large: `ARJUNA CHOOSES KRISHNA`

segments.voice: Settle, and fold your hands, the way Arjuna stands at the foot of the bed. Bring to mind something you're asking for these days, from a person or from life. Breathing in, name it plainly. Breathing out, ask underneath it: is this strength I can count, or a presence I want near? There's no wrong answer. Just let the question rest with your folded hands. If you pray, you can bring the asking into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Udyoga. Effort, getting ready: the book of the epic where both sides prepare, and Arjuna chooses Krishna over an army.
Your line: whose face Krishna saw when he opened his eyes. Today, when you choose between a person and an advantage, notice which one you reach for first. Day eight hundred thirteen.

howItsDone: Some Hindu teachers retell Arjuna's choice of Krishna over Krishna's army as a picture of devotion: choosing the Lord himself over what the Lord can give.

Krishna promised not to take up a weapon in the war

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. Krishna offers you first choice: a huge army, or Krishna himself, who will not fight. what do you choose?
options: the army; wars are won with soldiers.
ask to split the army instead.
fork.reveal: Arjuna chooses Krishna without hesitating, and Duryodhana happily takes the army.

original.note: effort, exertion, getting ready; the Udyoga Parva is the book of preparations before the war.

trapdoor: what you thought: Arjuna made a poor trade, one man for an army.
what it means: he chose the person over the power, and Krishna's presence matters more to him than numbers.
what a scholar hears: the scene is staged by position: the head of the bed and the foot, and whose face Krishna sees on waking.
recall: dark, in red, with a noose
waits for a lapse, then enters Nala

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva (Senodyoga), the council in Virata's hall and Duryodhana and Arjuna at Krishna's bedside in Dwaraka

notes: Audit: read against the Virata/Udyoga sequence in Ganguli as summarized; no factual, framing or repetition problem found; no change.
All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Balarama's counsel (conciliation; Yudhishthira gambled knowingly), Satyaki's angry reply, Drupada's advice to send an envoy and gather allies.

Confirm the bedside scene: Duryodhana arrives first and sits at the head; Arjuna at the feet with joined hands; Krishna sees Arjuna first and gives him first choice because he saw him first and he is the younger.
Krishna's army (the Narayanas) is described as huge without the number the text gives, under the claims rule.
Udyoga glossed as 'effort, getting ready' (a standard dictionary sense, not an etymology); a Keeper may refine.
howItsDone generalizes a devotional reading; check that it is fair across schools.
Editor: practice changed from gratitude for a steadying person (repeating days 800 and 804) to folded hands and a question about what one is asking for; howItsDone softened to 'some Hindu teachers'.
